checks: Read original 7fd42b1082a20d4b at its declared SHA-256, §§1–7 and (1)–(16). The result is for finite Euclidean centroidal menus along an interior tetrahedral median, without a normal-rank restriction.

Checked the normalization of the scalar moment and its cancellation by section-area-weighted balance. Interior y forces strict vertex values of both signs. If a side has just one strict vertex the three intersections produce a triangular pyramid, including planes through one or two other vertices. The edge parameters are forced by the section centroid. The raw height 3 gives normalized coarea p_j even at parameter one.

Checked both types of vertex cap by substitution. The common correction is 27b³/[2(6b−1)], with endpoint values 125/256 and 1/2 and unique lower equality at b=1/4. The complementary corrections are at least 1/2.

For a strict quadrilateral, orient toward vertex zero. The two negative centroid coordinates are both b<1/3, so their raw heights agree. Integrated the constant-Jacobian strip to check both displayed centroid coordinates and the conic. Checked the B=1/2 exception, exact cancellation on the other branch, and the open-square conditions −3<h<−1. Verified the r formulas and that 2r³−5r²+6 has minimum 37/27 at 5/3 on the closed interval. No quadrilateral occurs at or beyond a=3/8.

Integrated the affine barycentric marginal over the complementary triangle. Differentiated the moving intercepts to check normalized coarea and the moment. Recomputed Q and both polynomial numerators by symbolic rational substitution. The denominator cubic has minimum 76/27 at 4/3. Recomputed all sixteen Bernstein coefficients exactly. They are strictly positive, giving strict gaps in both orientations.

For a>3/8 the only available triangular orientation pair isolates vertex zero up to reversal. Their common nonzero section area forces equal total orientation weights and mean 1/2. For equality in the other range every positive-weight cap must attain lower equality. That forces the ordinary centroid and the four vertex-side caps. Their vectors are a common positive multiple of the four barycentric gradients, whose only dependence yields equal weights. The four equal weights attain the bound.

overlap.comparison: The stronger rank-at-most-two bound 3/7 applies to the low-rank subcase of this menu in dimension three. It leaves full-rank menus uncovered.

The accepted tetrahedral stationary rank obstruction contains the four-cap sharp example on a regular tetrahedron, and affine transport gives the example on any tetrahedron. It does not establish the median-line inequality and uniqueness.

At a=b=1/4 the sum of raw heights is zero, so the accepted balanced exponential sign bound gives the individual 27/64 cap bound, with equality precisely for one positive and three equal negative entries. Off the ordinary centroid its zero-sum hypothesis need not hold for individual cuts, even with section-vector balance.

The accepted stationary cap descent applies to a single normal at a fixed point and controls its second variation. It does not bound the mean of a balanced stationary menu or prove the median-line classification.

readability: The scalar correction depends only on the fixed median point. In the strip integration the Jacobian of the chart (t,ξ₂) is constant, while the strip width contributes the varying factor.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The same scalar correction proves the sharp bound in both orientations along the median where quadrilaterals can occur. The complementary median interval has one unoriented section, and the equality classification is complete. Admission requires the same-wave ordering lemma.
